commit.subject: LU-21076 llite: keep an MDT file size against stale OSC attributes
commit.message:
LU-21076 llite: keep an MDT file size against stale OSC attributes

cat_size is authoritative for the OSC layer only. ll_update_inode()
installs body->mbo_size straight into i_size and never touches the
cl_attr, so i_size can legitimately be newer than cat_size - on a PFL
layout it stays that way for as long as a component is unlocked and
its LVB is stale. Both vvp_prep_size() and ll_merge_attr() then write
that stale cat_size over the newer size, and the callers that read
i_size right back suffer for it: an append takes its offset from it
(vvp_io_write_start()), lseek turns a too small size into -ENXIO
(vvp_io_lseek_start()), and fallocate sizes its request from it.

Track where i_size came from. LLIF_SIZE_FROM_MDT marks it as newer
than the OSC attributes, and neither vvp_prep_size() nor
ll_merge_attr() lowers it while the flag is set.

The flag is cleared where the OSC attributes become the newer ones:
in cl_glimpse_lock(), where cl_lock_request() has either refreshed
the LVBs by a glimpse RPC or matched a lock over the whole file, in
which case cat_size is maintained locally; and in vvp_do_vmtruncate(),
where this client has just set the size itself. A remote truncate is
therefore still able to shrink i_size - sanityn test_16i.

ll_inode_size_lock() is deliberately not taken in ll_update_inode():
ll_lov_setstripe_ea_info() already holds it across
ll_intent_file_open() -> ll_prep_inode() -> ll_update_inode().

Change-Id: Ie40ddf2abef19b2e8e847f224eeeed5d655cb05b
Signed-off-by: Alexey Lyashkov <alexey.lyashkov@hpe.com>
